rules.name: Insurance start date
rules.statement: The pension fund insurance start date is derived from the latest first working day: if the first working day is the 1st of a month, insurance starts that day; otherwise on the 1st of the following month (e.g. 15.03.2026 → 01.04.2026). It is always the 1st of a month and is derived again whenever the first working day changes.

table.then: Insurance starts on the first working day
Insurance starts on the 1st of the following month

rules.name: Civil status for the pension fund
rules.statement: The civil status entered at the pension fund is taken from the employee's civil status; registered partnership and separated are provisionally entered as Married (with the spouse's/partner's date of birth).

rules.name: Civil status for source tax
rules.statement: For source tax, married and registered partnership count as 'married or registered partnership'; single, divorced, separated and widowed count as 'single, divorced, separated or widowed', as in the calculator.
rules.expression: if_else(civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"], "Married or registered partnership", if_else(is_set(civil_status), "Single, divorced, separated or widowed", null))

rules.name: Spouse exemption from source tax
rules.statement: An employee who is married or in a registered partnership with a spouse/partner who is Swiss or holds a C permit and lives in Switzerland is exempt from source tax.
rules.expression: civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and (spouse_nationality == "Swiss" or spouse_permit_type == "yes") and spouse_residence_country == "yes"

rules.name: Subject to source tax
rules.statement: An employee living abroad is always subject to source tax, whatever their nationality (also Swiss citizens). An employee living in Switzerland is subject only if not Swiss, without a C permit and without the spouse exemption. Only employees subject to source tax get the source tax questions.
rules.expression: address_country != "Switzerland" or (address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality == "Not Swiss" and permit_type == "no" and not spouse_exempts_source_tax)

rules.name: Residence for source tax
rules.statement: The calculator's residence answers are derived from the country of the home address: Switzerland (main residence in Switzerland), Germany, Liechtenstein, or any other country ('other country', which leaves the base tariff unchanged).
rules.expression: if_else(address_country == "Switzerland", "Switzerland", if_else(address_country in ["Germany", "Liechtenstein"], address_country, if_else(is_set(address_country), "Other country", null)))

rules.name: Church-tax suffix
rules.statement: The tariff code ends in Y for Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed, and in N for none or other.

when: Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed

rules.expression: if_else(confession == "Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed", "Y", if_else(confession == "None or other", "N", null))

rules.name: Base tariff letter for married employees
rules.statement: For married employees and registered partners subject to source tax: tariff letter C if the spouse/partner works or receives replacement income, otherwise B.
inputs: Spouse / partner works or receives replacement income

Cases the calculator exploration did not cover are 'not determined' until verified (OQ-child-paths-undetermined). The expression evaluates one child; the rule applies to each child.

rules.name: Tariff child digit
rules.statement: The tariff digit is the number of children who count (including H children); 0 without children. The expression covers a single child; with several children the counts are added up.

when: Counts or counts as H child

rules.expression: if_else(has_children == "yes" and child_tariff_result in ["counts", "counts as H child"], 1, 0)

rules.name: Single-parent tariff H
rules.statement: For a single, divorced, separated or widowed employee, any child counted as H child gives the H tariff overall (e.g. one A-counting and one H child → H2N).
inputs: Any child counts as H child
rules.expression: source_tax_civil_status == "Single, divorced, separated or widowed" and child_tariff_result == "counts as H child"

rules.name: Cross-border tariff applies
rules.statement: For employees living in Germany, the cross-border tariff applies with daily return and a certificate of residence ('not yet' counts as no), or without daily return when a daily return is reasonable and no more than 60 non-return days are expected. Every other case, and every other country, keeps the normal tariff.
rules.expression: source_tax_residence == "Germany" and ((daily_return_germany == "yes" and residence_certificate == "yes") or (daily_return_germany == "no" and daily_return_reasonable == "yes" and non_return_days_60 == "no"))

rules.name: Liechtenstein: in principle no source tax liability
rules.statement: An employee living in Liechtenstein who returns daily, or expects no more than 45 work-related non-return days, is in principle not liable to source tax, subject to the double taxation agreement. With more than 45 days the normal tariff code applies.

rules.name: Source tax tariff letter
rules.statement: Married/registered partners: C if the spouse works, else B. Single, divorced, separated or widowed: H with an H child, else A. If the cross-border tariff applies the letter becomes A→L, B→M, C→N, H→P.
rules.expression: if_else(source_tax_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership", if_else(spouse_employed == "yes", if_else(cross_border_tariff_applies, "N", "C"), if_else(spouse_employed == "no", if_else(cross_border_tariff_applies, "M", "B"), null)), if_else(source_tax_civil_status == "Single, divorced, separated or widowed", if_else(single_parent_h_tariff, if_else(cross_border_tariff_applies, "P", "H"), if_else(cross_border_tariff_applies, "L", "A")), null))

rules.name: Source tax result
rules.statement: For every employee subject to source tax Lonio computes the Zurich tariff code = tariff letter + child digit + church-tax suffix (e.g. C1Y, L0Y), replacing HR's manual calculator step; the result is recorded for HR. Liechtenstein residents with daily return or at most 45 non-return days get 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' instead, flagged for HR. Liechtenstein residents with more than 45 days get the normal code (the calculator adds 'subject to the double taxation agreement'). It is derived again from the latest answers whenever they change.

table.then: In principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement (flagged for HR)
Tariff code cannot be computed yet (OQ-child-paths-undetermined)
Tariff code: tariff letter + child digit + church-tax suffix

rules.expression: if_else(not subject_to_source_tax, "not subject to source tax", if_else(liechtenstein_no_source_tax_in_principle, "in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement", if_else(child_tariff_result == "not determined", "not determined", "tariff code")))

rules.name: Permit reminder
rules.statement: At the end of the questionnaire every non-Swiss employee and every employee living abroad (whatever their nationality, since it is not asked of them) is reminded to bring their permit on the first working day. HR words the reminder so that a Swiss citizen living abroad sees it does not apply to them. No data is collected.

rules.name: Discard answers that no longer apply
rules.statement: If the employee changes an earlier answer so that later questions no longer apply, those answers are discarded on submission (data minimisation); until submission they may be kept so that going back and forth loses no input. After submission the questionnaire is read-only for the employee; later changes are made by HR.

rules.name: Content of the employee's copy
rules.statement: If the employee asks for a copy, it is sent to the email address they typed in and shows the answers exactly as submitted, nothing more - no derived values such as the insurance start date or tariff code.

table.then: Send copy of submitted answers only

open_questions.question: What should be entered in the pension fund's required 'Canton' field for employees living abroad, and does 'Canton' mean canton of residence or of work?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The field is required and offers only the 26 Swiss cantons; cross-border employees (Germany, Liechtenstein) cannot be registered without a value. Provisionally only residents of Switzerland are asked (D-002).
options: Canton of work (Zurich) for employees abroad
Canton of residence; the fund gives a rule for employees abroad
HR enters a value agreed with the fund
